transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm just... having some trouble at work lately. I'm an electrician, and I just keep going back over my jobs. Checking the breakers, making sure the labels are right, looking at torque marks... I even take photos of everything, but sometimes I still end up driving back to a site just to be sure. It's making simple installs take a lot longer than they should. People are starting to notice, so... I figured I should come in.
Do you ever have thoughts or mental images that come into your mind that you don’t want there, that bother you or make you anxious?

Yeah, I guess so. It's... well, like I said, I check the panels and the disconnects. I know I checked them. But then... I don't know, this thought just pushes its way in. Like, what if I missed a loose neutral? What if I left something that could spark and start a fire? I try to just shake it off, you know, tell myself it's fine. But... it just kind of follows me. All the way home.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing certain things, like checking or taking photos, to try to reduce the anxiety or make sure everything is safe?

Yeah, I do. Like I mentioned before, I... I check the breakers and the torque marks. I take pictures on my phone so I can look at them later. But even with the photos, sometimes the feeling doesn't go away, and... I just end up driving back to the site to look at it in person. It's the only way to calm down.
Do you ever feel the need to do things in a certain way, like counting, repeating actions, or following strict routines, even if they don't directly relate to your worries about electrical safety?
No, not really. I mean... I don't count things or anything like that. It's just the work stuff. I just do my job.
When you go back to check the sites, is it mainly to make sure that nothing bad happens, like a fire or an accident, even though you know you already checked everything?

Yeah, I guess. It's just... I keep going over the jobs. Again and again. Checking the breakers, the labels, the torque marks. Looking at the photos. And like I said, sometimes driving back. It's... it makes a simple install take a lot longer than it should. People are starting to notice. That's... that's why I'm here.
When you go back to check the sites, is it mostly to make sure that nothing bad happens, like a fire or an accident, even though you already know you checked everything?

Yeah... it's like that. I know I checked the panel, or the disconnect. I know I did. But... the thought just barges in anyway. That maybe I missed a loose neutral, or... or left something that's gonna spark and start a fire. I try to shake it off, but... it just follows me all the way home.

When you have these thoughts about something going wrong, like a fire, does going back to check the site or taking photos feel like something you have to do to prevent something bad from happening, even if you know it's probably unnecessary?

Yeah. Like I was saying before... I just feel like I have to. If I don't go back and look at the breakers or the photos again, or drive back out there... I can't let it go. 

Even when I know the install is fine, I just... I keep doing it. I have to. And like I said, it's making everything take way too long. People at work are noticing, so... yeah. I just have to be sure.
Do these thoughts or checking behaviors affect parts of your life other than work, like your relationships, free time, or how you feel at home?

Yeah... I guess it does. 

My schedule is slipping. Jobs that should just be one visit... they turn into callbacks, or just me doing extra checks. It's costing me some client confidence, I think. And time I should be spending with the apprentices. 

And as for home... I don't really do much anymore. I've been skipping things I used to enjoy after work. I'm usually just... tied up reviewing the job in my head, or looking at the pictures, worrying if I need to drive back out there. So... yeah.
Do these thoughts about something going wrong feel intrusive and unwanted, and do you find them disturbing or hard to control, even though you know they might not make sense?

Yeah... I guess I already said that, but yeah. They just barge in. I'll know I checked the panel, I know it's fine, but... the thought about a loose neutral or a fire just pops up anyway. I try to shake it off, but... I can't really control it. It just follows me home.
